## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A single-fascicle Chen-dynasty Chinese translation of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā* by Paramārtha 真諦 (499–569 CE), the great Yogācāra translator. Signature: 「陳天竺三藏真諦譯」. For the *Diamond Sūtra* tradition broadly, see [T235](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023).

**Abstract**

T237 falls within Paramārtha's documented Chen-period activity (562–569 CE) at Yángzhōu and Guǎngzhōu. The translation is one of six Chinese versions of the *Vajracchedikā* ([T220](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0001)(9), [T235](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0023), [T236](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0024), [T237](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0026), [T238](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0027), [T239](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0028), [K016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0029)). Paramārtha's translation is the third Chinese rendering after [鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80) Kumārajīva and [菩提流支](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E6%94%AF) Bodhiruci, and the doublet relationships among the six Chinese versions have been a key topic in modern *Vajracchedikā* studies. Paramārtha is one of the most consequential Yogācāra translators in pre-Tang Chinese Buddhism, and his rendering reflects the Yogācāra-doctrinal reading of the *Diamond Sūtra* that became the doctrinal background of the *Mahāyāna-saṃparigraha* tradition.
